A_target.statement:
Let $f$ be [[Definition:Holomorphic Function|holomorphic]] on an open set containing the closed disk $\size {w - z_0} \le r$.
Then for $\size {z - z_0} < r$:
:$\displaystyle \map f z = \frac 1 {2 \pi i} \oint_{\size {w - z_0} \mathop = r} \frac {\map f w} {w - z} \rd w$

B_source.statement:
Let $g$ be [[Definition:Continuous Complex Function|continuous]] on an open disk $D$ and holomorphic on $D$ except possibly at one point.
Then $\displaystyle \oint_\gamma g = 0$ for every closed contour $\gamma$ in $D$.

substitutions.the function g: the difference quotient of f based at z

derived.vanishing of the integral of g: the integral of f(w)/(w - z) equals 2 pi i f(z)

object_map.reformulation: Subtract f(z) to make the integrand removable at z, so that Cauchy's theorem applies, and evaluate the remaining elementary integral.

validity_conditions: The difference quotient must extend continuously to z, which holds as f is differentiable there.
The circle has winding number 1 about z, giving the factor 2 pi i.
proof_plan:
Define:
:$\map g w = \begin {cases} \dfrac {\map f w - \map f z} {w - z} & : w \ne z \\ \map {f'} z & : w = z \end {cases}$
$g$ is continuous on a disk slightly larger than $\size {w - z_0} \le r$ and holomorphic away from $z$.

By the source result:
:$\displaystyle \oint_{\size {w - z_0} \mathop = r} \map g w \rd w = 0$

As $z$ lies inside the circle:
:$\displaystyle \oint_{\size {w - z_0} \mathop = r} \frac {\d w} {w - z} = 2 \pi i$

Hence:
:$\displaystyle \oint \frac {\map f w} {w - z} \rd w = \map f z \oint \frac {\d w} {w - z} = 2 \pi i \map f z$
which is [[Cauchy's Integral Formula]].
{{qed}}
